title: Stream ingest admission and live-edge tracking
name: Stream ingest limiter

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code enforces the maximum number of concurrent streams? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
In HighWaterMark::advance, compare_exchange_weak fails because another thread has meanwhile stored a larger media time. What happens next?
choices: advance returns false immediately without looking at the new value, because a failed exchange always means someone else won.
current is overwritten with the value actually found in value_, the while condition is re-evaluated against it, and advance returns false if the found value is not smaller than candidate.
The loop spins forever, because current is never updated when the exchange fails.
value_ is overwritten with candidate anyway, because the success order is acq_rel.

questions.prompt: IngestService::snapshot() reads segments_in_, bytes_in_, the limiter counters and the live edge with separate loads. What can a monitoring thread observe?
choices: A torn 64-bit value on 32-bit platforms, because the counters are plain integers wrapped in std::atomic only for increments.
Values that are always mutually consistent, because the acquire load in HighWaterMark::get() orders all the earlier relaxed loads.
Stale values from before the last segment, because relaxed counters are only published when a thread exits.
Each field is individually exact, but the fields need not come from the same instant, so bytes and segments may not match what any single moment looked like.

questions.prompt: Two publisher threads call IngestService::accept_segment at the same moment. The sequencer uses fetch_add with memory_order_relaxed. What does that guarantee?
choices: The two threads receive distinct sequence numbers, but relaxed ordering says nothing about how this operation is ordered relative to other memory accesses in either thread.
The two threads may receive the same sequence number, because relaxed operations are not required to agree on a single order for one variable.
The thread that receives the lower sequence number is guaranteed to have its live-edge update and byte count visible to the other thread first.
The numbers are distinct only because accept_segment is called from threads that each hold a StreamPermit.
